headline: Brentford lose two midfielders — and still head to Hull as favourites
summary: Brentford are sixth in the Premier League and travel to Hull City on Sunday, but they do it without Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt, both sent off in the second half against Liverpool. Hull are winless in five and created only 0.16 expected goals at Fulham, a first half their manager called one of the worst since he took charge. Yet the price went the other way: across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Brentford's fair win chance rose from 53.3% to 54.8%. The handicap gives Hull a head start of 0.75 goals, and the goal line sits at 2.75, with over at 51.8%.
read: Brentford are clear favourites at Hull — 54.8% to win and rated about 0.7 goals the better side — after taking 10 points from their first seven games, even with Yarmolyuk and Janelt suspended. Hull are winless in five and created just 0.16 xG at Fulham, a performance their manager called one of the worst halves of his reign.

facts.fact: Brentford are without Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt, both sent off in the second half of their home defeat to Liverpool.
facts.meaning: Two midfielders unavailable for the trip to Hull, so Brentford's central options are thinner than in their sixth-placed start.

facts.fact: The market makes Brentford 54.8% favourites to win at Hull.
facts.meaning: Clear away favourites — more than double Hull's 21.3% chance of a home win.

facts.fact: Hull City are winless in five matches — two draws and three defeats.
facts.meaning: The home side go into a visit from a top-six team without a win in their last five outings.

facts.fact: Hull created just 0.16 xG at Fulham on Saturday.
facts.meaning: Almost nothing created in their most recent game — the attack, not just the result, is the concern going into this one.

facts.fact: Sergej Jakirović said Hull's first half at Fulham was one of the worst halves of football he has seen since taking charge.
facts.meaning: A manager publicly calling out his team — the home side arrives under pressure to produce a response.

facts.fact: The market's fair handicap line is Hull +0.72, rating Brentford about 0.7 goals the better side.
facts.meaning: A Brentford win is expected, but not a comfortable one — on the -0.75 line the two sides are close to a coin flip.

facts.fact: Igor Thiago has one goal and one assist in seven Premier League games this season.
facts.meaning: Brentford's striker is short of goals going into a game they are expected to win.

facts.fact: Brentford have conceded 1.62 xG per game across their last five matches.
facts.meaning: The sixth-placed side gives up more chance quality than it creates — the position is built on results rather than control.

sources.fact: Brentford will be without two key players for Sunday's trip to Hull City.
Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were both sent off in the second half of Brentford's defeat to Liverpool, leaving them suspended for the Hull game.
Brentford sit sixth in the Premier League table with 10 points from seven fixtures.
Brentford have two wins, four draws and one defeat from their opening seven league games.
Igor Thiago has scored just one goal and provided one assist in seven Premier League games this season ahead of the trip to Hull.
Brentford issued a club statement and are supporting a police investigation after an item was kicked from a height towards the pitch during Saturday's match against Liverpool.
Hull City are on a run of two consecutive away defeats after losing 1-0 at Fulham.
Sergej Jakirović told his players their first half at Fulham was one of the worst halves of football he has seen since taking charge, a view one player said he totally agreed with.
